title: Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa
hook: a queen's strange illness, a cure no one could fetch, and a boy who rides home on a tigress

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa: a baby with a bell at his neck, found by the Pampa river and raised by the king of Pandalam as Manikandan.

The prescription is impossible on purpose. The queen of Pandalam lies in a darkened room, clutching her head. The palace physician bows and gives his verdict: only one cure will work, the milk of a tigress. The room goes silent. Nobody walks into the forest and milks a tiger, and the physician knows it. Because the illness, in the story, isn't real. It's a plan to send someone into the forest who isn't supposed to come back. Today, the boy who went anyway.
screen: `AN IMPOSSIBLE CURE` → `THE MILK OF A TIGRESS` → `AN ILLNESS THAT ISN'T REAL`

segments.voice: In the telling, after the king adopts Manikandan, the queen has a son of her own. A scheming minister whispers to her that the adopted boy will take the throne from her child. Afraid, she agrees to pretend to be ill, and the physician is in on it. It's an old human fear, the kind that makes ordinary people do things they later regret. Manikandan is still young. He hears what the cure is, and he offers to go. The king begs him not to. The boy goes anyway, alone, into the forest, with a bundle of food for the road. The story doesn't make him angry, and it doesn't make him suspicious. He simply goes to fetch what his mother says she needs. In the forest, tradition says, Manikandan meets the demoness Mahishi and overcomes her, which was why he was born. Then he comes home, not with a pot of milk, but riding on a tigress, with a band of tigers walking behind him. In some tellings the tigers are gods in disguise. The palace gate is full of terrified people. The queen and the minister, seeing him, understand what they've done, and fall at his feet asking forgiveness. And the king finally understands who his son is. The story puts its weight not on punishment for the plotters, but on what the boy does with their plot: he turns a trap into an errand of care, and comes back with more than they asked for.
screen: `A PLAN BORN OF FEAR` · `THE BOY GOES ANYWAY` · `HOME ON A TIGRESS` · `THE PLOTTERS ASK FORGIVENESS`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one task ahead that feels set up to go badly, a hard meeting, a difficult conversation, a job nobody else wanted, and feel the weight of it. Then picture yourself setting out toward it calmly, a bundle on your shoulder, breathing in steadiness and breathing out suspicion. If you pray, you can say Ayyappa's name softly with each breath.
Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa. Today, the tiger's milk: a cure meant as a trap, a boy who went anyway, and his return on a tigress. Today's word.
